newsitem.title: NORWAY: Norway shares end flat, Storebrand buyer revealed.
newsitem.headline: Norway shares end flat, Storebrand buyer revealed.

text.p: A slow Norwegian share market picked up activity on Friday after the release of key U.S. unemployment data, but closed unchanged from the previous session.
Oslo's Total share index finished 0.05 percent up at 1,095.75 points, the fourth consecutive close in positive territory.
Turnover amounted to 1.26 billion crowns, but included the 410 million crown sale of a block of shares in real estate group Avantor ASA by industrial holding company Aker RGI ASA .
Trade was once again swift in Norway's largest insurance company Storebrand ASA, which advanced 0.90 crowns to 47.70 crowns in business worth 95.6 million crowns.
Storebrand's share price has risen sharply from 42.50 crowns on February 25, as a mystery buyer hunted on the market for large amounts of stock.

Norwegian billionaire entrepreneur Kjell Inge Roekke said in a statement on Friday he had bought around six percent of the company through his private Liberian-registered company Ivory Enterprises Corp. Roekke said the purchase was a private investment. --Oslo newsroom, +47 22 42 50 41
